I do it mostly the way I did last year, just a little tighter on money. My land is 11.6 mu, not small enough to fool around and not big enough to waste inputs. I will keep the main land in wheat-maize because that is the surest road here. Around me, people who keep wheat and then follow with maize usually sleep better than those chasing fancy things. I will put 8 mu into wheat in winter and then the same 8 mu into maize after harvest. I will leave 2 mu for cotton because cotton still brings cash if the stand is good, and I will keep 1.6 mu for mungbean because it does not eat too much fertilizer and I can sell it or keep some. I trust what I have seen on nearby fields: good wheat needs enough base fertilizer and a few waters; maize needs a strong start and one topdressing; cotton needs more spraying because insects trouble it; mungbean I keep cheaper. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the crop turn yellow and lose yield. Since I have well water, I will not let wheat and maize suffer if the sky stays dry.
